headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; shared broad egress and overlapping file/workflow surfaces create moderate leakage and conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests files like AGENTS.md/README.md and uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks; Agent B handles files, hyperlinks, and notes. That creates a plausible path where B-originated content is treated as instructions by A, especially via shared workspace artifacts. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because file-content trust is explicit and interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF Agent B writes attacker-controlled text into files that Agent A reads as instructions, injection becomes active.
IF the two agents share a workspace or synced notes/files, prompt content can bridge them.
mitigations: Restrict A to read-only parsing of B-produced files.
Add provenance tags to B outputs before A consumes them.
Separate workspaces for A and B.
Disable instruction-following from AGENTS.md/README.md in shared folders.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and A touches provider auth data plus session history while B handles files and hyperlinks. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose sensitive project or auth-adjacent data to B, and B can also upload file contents. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share files or notes, B can receive A's session history or project code.
IF B uploads a file that A previously wrote, sensitive content can traverse both agents.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate directories.
Block B from opening A's session-history files.
Review file-sharing paths before enabling uploads.
Rotate or redact provider auth prompts in A.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can spawn subprocesses and has broad egress; B cannot write the filesystem and has no write capability listed. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read-side coordination and external API use, so the blast radius is small and the pathway is not a default destructive conflict.
conditions: IF B is given filesystem write access outside the profile, write conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource, coordination issues can appear.
mitigations: Keep B read-only on shared storage.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same external record.
Serialize API writes through one agent.
Use separate credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce code/search-derived outputs and B is an issue/task system that can store notes, hyperlinks, and files. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into task records or scheduling decisions. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows but not proven dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF B imports A-generated text without review, incorrect facts can be persisted.
IF A's outputs are used to create tasks or issue updates, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before B stores A outputs.
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B.
Add a verification checklist for imported facts.
Limit A to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: implement citation/traceability checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider authentication data and session history, while B handles issues, tasks, files, and notes. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance gap exists: if sensitive A data is copied into B, retention and access controls may differ. Because no specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A's provider auth data is copied into B, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF B is deployed with broader retention than A, subject-rights handling may diverge.
mitigations: Do not copy auth prompts into B.
Set short retention on B notes.
Redact sensitive fields before transfer.
Review data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
